title: My take on a Babylon-themed Action Roguelite using Claude Code, 2 months in
author: Cosmonan
selftext: Been working on an Action Roguelite set in Babylon, taking inspiration from games like Nier Automata and DMC. I'm now implementing an elemental combo system. So far I've been using Claude Code with Unity, and sometimes Laguna S2.1 from VS Code / Cline when I run out of Claude tokens. Wanted to hear opinions from you guys, what do you think? Any tips?

comments.author: kilographix
comments.body: Looks really cool! I would like to know a bit more abour your asset pipeline!

replies.author: Cosmonan
replies.body:
It's currently a mix of everything tbh:

Free from Asset Store: item icons, some VFX, destructible props (tables, boxes, etc)

Paid 3P: animation pack, elemental VFX and some textures

Level geometry: self made tileset that is combined on runtime to generate the level.

I don't really have any AI generated assets now. I've been using AI mostly for teaching me Unity and writing scripts for the systems. I don't really touch any code, but I do work inside Unity after Claude teaches me some stuff, like Animator and some prefabs editing.

I usually create a system with a single example asset, like an apple for inventory system, and from that on Claude has context to add more assets to said system.

replies.author: anubis_is_watching
replies.body:
Sounds like my exact workflow! Glad to see someone else has made it work. 

I created a prototype last summer and left it but picked it back up recently, tightening all the original systems up.

Yours looks great so far! Cheers and good luck!

replies.author: Cosmonan
replies.body:
Good to hear you are back to the project! Any plans on sharing some gameplay here? 

Yep, this workflow seems like a good balance of AI work while I keep in control of the big scheme.

replies.author: anubis_is_watching
replies.body:
Yeah I think so! I hope to make some decent progress balancing everything else over the next six months. Got a lot to learn but it’s a labor of love. 

I hope to pay homage to and satiate a craving for those who miss the Nier: Automata and Replicant scale and vibes. Although far different from your own design and style. 

Gotta say I love similar inspiration in yours as well!

replies.author: Cosmonan
replies.body:
Okay, you got me interested big time! Do you plan on making a linear game or some sort of roguelite as well?

Nier is such a good reference for character animation. I don't know, but the way 2B moves feels so natural and responsive, I wish I could translate some of that juiceness to my game. 

My first decisive moment was learning about Root Motion. That alone made me move from Godot to Unity, which handles this in a much easier way. No regrets so far.

replies.author: anubis_is_watching
replies.body:
Yeah man, kinda! Linear main story with multiple endings derived based on calculated average of choices — similar to like the karma system. Then after the final section is completed, there’s an epilogue state that provides the end section to be eternally ran as a rogue-lite. 

I’ll be honest, I’ve not messed with character anims at all beyond extremely rudimental ones currently. My primary focus has been story, level design, player progression, and atmosphere. I’ll refine character design and dev at a far later stage. 

I need to look into Root Motion though, I’m honestly unfamiliar with that right now. 

Have you used Unity’s AI? I’ve actually heard some decent things about it. 

Sounds like im very green compared to you. But im trying my best!! lol

replies.author: Cosmonan
replies.body:
I like the roguelite as endgame mechanic, reminds me of Dragons Dogma Dark Arisen, very nice feature! 

Root Motion is basically making the animation move your character through a root bone, no the other way around. Makes the character move more fluidly.

Your primary focuses are exactly what I'm missing RN lol. So far I've only been able to tackle combat, skill, inventory and atribute systems... My bro is supposed to work on story, setting, npcs and models, but hasn't made much so far, anyways it's a passion project so I'm also not putting any pressure.

What do you mean by Unity AI? I've been using Claude Code only, and just discovered I wasnt using MCP at all hahaha, so things might go faster now it's enabled. Also planning on using the CLI routing I saw in some videos.

replies.author: anubis_is_watching
replies.body:
Thanks man! You know in gotta check out Dragons Dogma I’ve heard great things about it! 

Oh that’s super cool. I definitely do need to check that out. I’ve officially learned something very useful here lol. I have a lot of enemies that sound like they’d benefit from that. 

Sounds like we’re opposites! lol. I love world building so if you ever want to bounce ideas around let me know! 

As of like 6 I think? Unity introduced their AI. Here’s a link:

If you’re not sure about the link honestly I just grabbed the official page so you can search it yourself.   
But it’s built for Unity by them trained of their native architecture. I have been ironing out my workflow and will be likely using this for some procedural gen code of a few areas as well as some simple anims..

Is yours planned to be like a tower clear? Like each level gets progressively harder?

replies.author: Cosmonan
replies.body:
Okay this looks promising, I'm testing right now by trying to build a Hub Scene better than the one that I have.

Yes, basically a tower clear, each level gets harder, every 5 levels a boss, and some objecties each floor. After dying you get some coins based on the combo score for the run, which you use to unlock meta progression: elements, combo movements, skills and attribute bonuses. I plan to have some more tileset diversity as well, for different floor layouts.

comments.author: Excellent_Resolve871
comments.body:
This looks amazing for 2 months in! Aside from the UI, this doesn't obviously appear AI generated.

Very interested in the art side of your workflows. Are these all 3P assets? If not, what's your workflow for generating these assets?

Also interested in your level design and production workflows. Did AI design this level? Did Claude also populate it?

replies.author: Cosmonan
replies.body:
Thank youuu, it's been some intense work during this time, but I feel this is paying off.

Assets are a mix of everything;

3P: animation pack, some vfx, icons, texture pack

Self made: Tileset (walls and floor)

Basically the levels are procedurally generated in runtime (the technique is called WFC) and filled with my tileset, which edit by hand inside Unity. Since Babylon is full of geometric forms, it is easily doable inside Unity iself.

I can't recommend Smart Textures pack from Free Stylized enough, you can easily edit the materials, changing color, tile size, roughness and everything with sliders. I believe it's 5$ or something for the monthly subscription, qnd you have access to 100s of smart materials.

comments.author: PykeTheTitan
comments.body: Looks solid, what are you using for animation?

replies.author: Cosmonan
replies.body:
I got a 2h greatsword animation pack from Unity Asset Store. The workflow then follows:

I tell Claude which animation prefab I want to use, and for what, it creates the C# side, and gives me the instructions to create the state transition in the Animation Window inside Unity. From that I adjust the animatikn transition to my likings.

comments.author: dont-pull-a-druckman
comments.body: Looks good, but god is this style of game/combat so tiring. Every game does this shit now lol

replies.author: Cosmonan
replies.body:
Thank you! What exactly about the combat do you find tiring? It's basically classic action combat from the original GoW franchise and things like that, kinda satistying tbh. My idea is for the combo movements to open up as you advance. 

As for the elemental combo, you can equip 2 elements to your attacks (Square and Triangle) before a run (Fire and Thunder in the video). Attacking an enemy will eventually afflict them with the attacking element, and attacking with a second element triggers the combo: Fire + Thunder = Explosion. I will add Earth/Desert next, giving me Magma and Magnetic combos.

comments.author: Zennity
comments.body:
I know its a demo, but i think the audio sfx should be a priority rn. Maybe reduce the hitstop values a tad as well like on the spin attack? The song for the level is also so generic… ik its babylonian themed but… its uninspiring to me personally. 

Now the good parts: it looks good. Seems like the major systems are in place and work. Combat wise? You said dmc so…. I need more style and jump cancels lmao. I don’t think enough is shown here to really critique. As it stands honestly i like it but at the same time it also feels generic. 

Any plans for a parry/perfect dodge system?

replies.author: Cosmonan
replies.body:
Thanks for the feedback! Yep, SFX and music have just been thrown in TBH, gotta do some polishing, and you are right, it is a priority now. 

I wish I could attain DMC levels of combos, but I'm not sure I will be able to that single handedly hahaha, and animation is mostly manual work, AI won't help much with that. I wish to add some grapple system, but that would be too generic, so I'm still thinking about some additional movement system.

Perfect Dodge is already implemented, but not perfected (no pun intended lol). Enemies glow red during wind up (gotta add some proper VFX for that), and if you dodge during that time window you have a time slowdown and recharge energy. I ended up not showing this feature in tne video, but needs refining anyways. I don't have any plans for adding parry on the other hand.

replies.author: Zennity
replies.body:
Nvidia recently released a way to generate animations with an AI model named kimodo. I havent dived into it myself honestly but maybe it can help with animation work? Getting DMC level of action is a huge task lmao so i was saying it half-jokingly. 

This game reminds me of godbreakers, not sure if you ever saw it but it also has a grapple system. Maybe take a look at it if you haven’t heard of it. 

Wish i had more constructive things to share. If you have time, maybe you should make a demo of the roguelite progression as well in a run and outside of it. That’s what keeps us coming back in this genre.

replies.author: Cosmonan
replies.body:
Hmm seems like a good idea, I will check that out, maybe this Kimodo helps me increasing my combo roster. Will also check Godbreakers, and no, I have never heard about that 😊. You did have some good shared stuff, man, some of this will certainly guide me on a better path. Thank you!!

Also, playable demo in a couple months, maybe? Let's see...
